title: Symmetry-guided construction and exact certification of absolutely maximally entangled states
abstract: We construct Hermitian self-dual maximum-distance-separable codes with parameters $[12,6,7]_{25}$, $[18,9,10]_{121}$, and $[18,9,10]_{169}$. Through the nonbinary stabilizer construction these codes define $\text{AME}(12,5)$, $\text{AME}(18,11)$, and $AMD(18,13)$ states, and one-party projection gives $\text{AME}(17,11)$ and $\text{AME}(17,13)$. The $[12,6,7]_{25}$ code, which is not monomially equivalent to a generalized Reed-Solomon code, is obtained by a systematic search without prescribed coordinate symmetry; its monomial-semilinear automorphism group acts with a regular $\mathbb{Z}_3^2$ orbit on nine coordinates. Imposing that action on two nine-coordinate orbits reduces the length-eighteen search to a nine-element group algebra kernel, whose Hermitian character decomposition splits the invariant self-duality constraints into independent blocks with exact family counts; a norm-one coordinate scaling removes a factor $q+1=14$ at $q=13$. Hermitian self-duality and the MDS property are certified by exact field arithmetic and complete square-minor enumeration. Graph-state cut-rank computations, including all single-vertex deletions of the length-eighteen graphs, provide additional exact checks.
summary: This paper constructs and rigorously certifies several Absolutely Maximally Entangled (AME) quantum states by linking them to specific Hermitian self-dual Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes. The methodology combines systematic computational searches with advanced algebraic tools like character decomposition to ensure the mathematical exactness of the results. It advances the theoretical understanding of highly entangled quantum resources.
main_problem: The primary goal is the construction and exact certification of Absolutely Maximally Entangled (AME) quantum states.
main_result: The authors explicitly construct and certify several AME states, including $	ext{AME}(12, 5)$, $	ext{AME}(18, 11)$, and $	ext{AME}(18, 13)$, using specific Hermitian self-dual Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes.
method: The methods involve advanced techniques from coding theory, specifically utilizing systematic searches combined with imposing symmetry constraints ($\mathbb{Z}_3$ action) and employing character decomposition of group algebras for rigorous verification.
model_or_system: The physical system is defined by quantum states represented as graph states derived from Hermitian self-dual codes over finite fields $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. The state space is $(\mathbb{C}^q)^{\otimes n}$.
key_observables: AME parameters, such as the code dimensions $[n, k, d]$ (e.g., $[12, 6, 7]_{25}$), and graph-state cut-rank computations.
important_parameters: The field size $q$ (e.g., 5, 11, 13) and the number of parties $n$ are critical parameters defining the state structure.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on establishing exact mathematical conditions for self-duality and MDS properties via field arithmetic and complete square-minor enumeration; limitations exist regarding whether the found solutions represent all possible codes in their class.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the two-stage search pipeline, geometric constraints imposed by symmetry (e.g., group-circulant forms), and summaries of existence maps for AME states across various parameters.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure moving from defining the problem (AME states via MDS codes) to developing sophisticated algebraic tools (symmetry imposition, character decomposition) used in a systematic search pipeline to yield explicit constructions and rigorous certifications for specific parameter sets.
why_interesting: This work provides deep connections between abstract algebra (coding theory over finite fields) and fundamental quantum information concepts like entanglement measures, which is highly relevant for theoretical quantum computation research.
